class.name: PlayFabPartyConfig
class.brief_description: Configuration for [PlayFabParty] initialization and network create/join.
class.description: Optional configuration for [method PlayFabParty.initialize_async], [method PlayFabParty.create_and_join_network_async], and [method PlayFabParty.join_network_async]. Chat-related fields are addon policy flags; they decide whether and how the addon creates and connects Party chat controls and are not native Party network settings.

members.member: Maximum number of players permitted in the Party network.

Direct peer connectivity policy bitmask. See [enum PlayFabParty.DirectPeerConnectivity]. Defaults to [constant PlayFabParty.DIRECT_PEER_CONNECTIVITY_NONE] (all traffic relayed through PlayFab Party). Platform-type and entity-login-provider flags must be combined; for the common "any platform + any login provider" preset use [constant PlayFabParty.DIRECT_PEER_CONNECTIVITY_ANY]. Invalid combinations cause [method PlayFabParty.create_and_join_network_async] to fail synchronously with code [code]party_invalid_options[/code].
Optional invitation id; the addon generates one if empty.
Whether the addon should create and connect a voice chat control.
Whether the addon should enable text chat on the chat control.

Whether the addon should enable speech-to-text transcription on the chat control. When [code]true[/code] the addon calls [code]SetTranscriptionOptions[/code] on the local chat control for the local user plus all remote controls, in both matching and non-matching languages, so [signal PlayFabPartyChat.transcription_received] fires.

Whether the addon should enable translation on the chat control. Translation is receiver-side in PlayFab Party: when [code]true[/code] the addon asks Party to translate incoming text chat (and, when [member enable_transcription] is also set, incoming transcriptions) into this control's language, surfaced as [member PlayFabPartyChatMessage.translated_text].

Audio input (microphone) device id bound on the local chat control. Empty selects the platform's system default communication device. The device is always bound when the chat control is created; whether voice actually flows still depends on chat permissions and the audio subsystem successfully initializing the chosen device.

Audio output (speaker) device id bound on the local chat control. Empty selects the platform's system default communication device. The device is always bound when the chat control is created; whether voice actually flows still depends on chat permissions and the audio subsystem successfully initializing the chosen device.

BCP-47 language code applied to the local chat control at creation. Empty keeps the Party default (the platform's language). This is the language used for outgoing text chat and voice transcription, and the target language for receiver-side translation.
